requirements.description: Normal diffs do not own, recreate, or drop Supabase-managed schemas and objects.
Supported hooks, policies, triggers, grants, publications, and wrappers survive managed boundaries.
Platform-managed catalog changes do not create spurious application migrations.
Extension absence, version mismatch, and local-hosted differences produce explicit diagnostics.
RLS covers uid, jwt, claims, MFA/AAL, anonymous identities, and organization membership.
Auth hooks retain exact ownership, grants, and configuration.
Auth user triggers, profile mirrors, cascades, hardened search paths, and failure behavior are preserved.
Supabase database roles retain least-privilege boundaries.
Auth records and provider state are service fixtures and never migration data.
Bucket and object policies cover visibility, ownership, folders, type, size, signed operations, and service roles.
Application tables safely reference Storage identifiers through supported helpers.
Bucket metadata and object bytes are service data rather than pg-delta output.
Realtime publication membership, filters, columns, replica identity, RLS, and grants evolve safely.
Broadcast and Presence authorization policies evolve safely.
Database broadcast triggers and topic or payload helpers evolve safely.
Channel subscriptions and messages are verified as runtime behavior, not DDL.
pg_net webhook trigger lifecycle, payloads, headers, timeout, and failure behavior are covered.
Vault-backed webhook credentials are retained and fully redacted.
Environment-specific URLs and configuration do not destabilize schema diffs.
Edge Function source, JWT behavior, deployment, invocation, and versioning remain outside pg-delta DDL.

requirements.section: Vault, Cron, Queues, and background work
requirements.description: Vault wrappers, ACLs, rotation, deletion, and secret non-disclosure are covered.

requirements.section: Vault, Cron, Queues, and background work
requirements.description: Cron schedules and job history respect the schema-runtime boundary.

requirements.section: Vault, Cron, Queues, and background work
requirements.description: Queue lifecycle, RLS, grants, archive state, and messages respect the schema-runtime boundary.

requirements.section: Vault, Cron, Queues, and background work
requirements.description: Cross-feature background processing flows preserve each service boundary.
pgvector dimensions, operators, HNSW, IVFFlat, wrappers, changes, and upgrades are covered.
PostGIS types, SRIDs, indexes, generated geography, availability, and upgrades are covered.
pg_graphql directives, relationships, inflection, and schema-cache behavior are covered.
Wrappers and FDWs cover options, Vault credentials, unavailable remotes, and foreign tables.
Common Supabase extensions interact safely across availability and upgrade boundaries.
PostgREST exposure covers schemas, grants, RLS, views, RPCs, relationships, comments, and cache reload.
Supabase configuration variants are exercised without confusing configuration with DDL.
Multiple declarative files, ordering, duplicates, deletion, parse failure, and drift are covered.
Local reset and protected linked, preview, repair, and squash workflows are covered.
Seeds are idempotent and remain separate from declarative schema changes.
CLI and pg-delta versions, feature flags, cleanup, interruption, offline behavior, and diagnostics are covered.
